title: Victoria residential — houses, townhouses and apartments
description: ARBV-aligned stages from pre-design through post-occupancy, with Clause 54 / 55 / 58, Better Apartments Design Standards (BADS) on apartment items, NCC 2025 (in force in Victoria from 1 May 2026), and apartment developer-bond notes.

stages.title: Pre-design
stages.summary: Brief, title, planning context, budget and what is possible on the site before sketching.

stages.title: Concept / sketch design
stages.summary: Options, massing and a preferred concept the client can sign, tested against Vic planning and 7-star orientation.

stages.title: Design development
stages.summary: Resolve the preferred scheme with consultants, materials, ESD and amenity so it is ready to lodge.

stages.title: Town planning
stages.summary: Confirm whether a planning permit is required and run Clause 54, 55 or 58 through to endorsed plans.

stages.title: Construction documentation
stages.summary: Working drawings and specifications that match endorsed planning drawings and NCC 2025 for a building permit.

stages.title: Tender and contractor selection
stages.summary: Issue the tender set, compare builders, and appoint under a written building contract.

stages.title: Building contract administration
stages.summary: Building permit, inspections, variations, progress certificates, and occupancy.

stages.title: Practical completion
stages.summary: Inspect, list defects, collect keys and manuals, and certify practical completion.

stages.title: Defects liability (post-occupancy)
stages.summary: Track and close defects during the contractual DLP and any apartment bond inspections.

stages.title: Final certificate
stages.summary: Issue the final certificate after DLP, start domestic building warranties, and archive the record.

stages.title: Post-occupancy evaluation
stages.summary: Seasonal comfort, energy, landscape and lessons learned after people have lived in the building.

items.title: Confirm architect registration
items.detail: Check the architect (and any company) is registered with the Architects Registration Board of Victoria before engagement.
references: Victorian Architects Code of Professional Conduct

items.title: Written client–architect agreement
items.detail: Do not start work until a written agreement is signed. Record stages, fees, consultants, and whether planning and contract administration are included.

items.title: Project brief
items.detail: Record household or dwelling mix, accessibility, working from home, storage, parking, landscape, budget range, and must-not-change constraints.

items.title: Title, easements, covenants and restrictions
items.detail: Obtain a current title, plan of subdivision, easements, covenants, S173 agreements, and any owners corporation rules that constrain siting or materials.

items.title: Owners corporation and common property
items.detail: Identify OC plan, common property, exclusive-use areas, and whether a special resolution is needed for works.

items.title: Zone, overlays and planning scheme
items.detail: Record municipality, planning scheme, zone, overlays (heritage, flood, bushfire, special building, DDO, SLO, HO, BMO, LSIO, SBO) and whether a planning permit is likely.

items.title: Applicable residential clause
items.detail: House or small second dwelling: Clause 54 if a planning permit is required. Two or more dwellings / townhouses / low-rise apartments to three storeys: Clause 55 (Townhouse and Low-Rise Code). Apartments of five storeys or more: Clause 58. Confirm storeys and dwelling count.

items.title: BADS — which clause applies
items.detail: Better Apartments Design Standards (BADS) apply to apartment buildings. Use Clause 55.07 for apartments under five storeys (and Clause 55 / the Townhouse and Low-Rise Code if the building is three storeys or less). Use Clause 58 for five storeys or more, excluding a basement, and for apartments in commercial, activity-centre and similar zones. Record storeys excluding basement.

items.title: Feature and level survey
items.detail: Commission a site survey with levels, trees, crossovers, services, adjoining windows and secluded private open space relevant to ResCode.
references: VPP cl 54.01 / 55.01 neighbourhood and site description

items.title: Services and authority constraints
items.detail: Locate sewer, stormwater, water, power, gas, NBN, and any build-over or asset-protection requirements. Flag septic or unsewered lots.

items.title: Bushfire, flood, contamination and heritage
items.detail: Record BAL if BMO or BAL construction may apply, flood levels, heritage citation, and potential contamination on infill lots.

resources.label: CFA — building in a bushfire area

items.title: Budget, program and GST
items.detail: Set a working construction budget, consultant budget, authority fees, and a program that includes planning time. Note GST treatment.
references: A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Act 1999 (Cth)

items.title: Neighbourhood context photos
items.detail: Photograph streetscape, adjoining dwellings, existing trees, and likely overlooking/overshadowing interfaces.
references: VPP cl 54.01 / 55.01 neighbourhood and site description

items.title: Site analysis
items.detail: Sun path, prevailing wind, views, privacy, significant trees, slope, and street character. This feeds the design response.

items.title: Concept options
items.detail: Issue at least one preferred sketch scheme (and alternatives if the agreement requires). Record client comments against each.

items.title: Height, setbacks and garden area
items.detail: Test building height, street setback, site coverage, permeability and garden-area requirements of the zone before locking a plan.

items.title: Clause 55 deemed-to-comply check
items.detail: Run an early check against street setback, height, side/rear setbacks, walls on boundaries, site coverage, access, tree canopy and front fence. Flag where the Townhouse and Low-Rise Code deemed-to-comply path is intended.
references: Clause 55 Townhouse and Low-Rise Code (from 31 March 2025)

items.title: Tree canopy target
items.detail: Design for 10% canopy cover on sites up to 1,000 m² and 20% above 1,000 m², counting existing trees where they will be retained.

items.title: BADS — dwelling mix and street interface
items.detail: Developments of ten or more dwellings should provide a range of dwelling sizes. Orient the building to the street; avoid blank walls, high front fences, and waste or carpark entries that dominate the street (Clause 58.02 / 55.07).

items.title: BADS — communal open space
items.detail: Ten or more dwellings: at least 30 m² of communal outdoor open space. Thirteen or more: an extra 2.5 m² per dwelling or 220 m², whichever is less (indoor or outdoor). Locate communal outdoor space on the north side where practical, with winter solar access (Clause 58.03-2 / 58.03-3).

items.title: BADS — private open space and balconies
items.detail: Give every dwelling secluded private open space to the BADS table (area and minimum dimension). Add 1.5 m² if a condenser sits on the balcony. South-facing living balconies may be 1.2 m deep; north-facing may be 1.7 m. Above about 40 m, extra living-room area can substitute for balcony area.

items.title: BADS — functional layout
items.detail: Main bedroom at least 3 m × 3.4 m (10.2 m²). Other bedrooms at least 3 m × 3 m (9 m²). Living rooms: studio/one-bed 3.3 m wide and 10 m²; two or more bedrooms 3.6 m wide and 12 m² (Clause 58.07-1).

items.title: BADS — room depth and windows
items.detail: Single-aspect habitable rooms should not be deeper than 2.5 times the ceiling height. Open-plan single-aspect rooms may be up to 9 m where the ceiling is at least 2.7 m. Every habitable room needs a window in an external wall — not borrowed light from a corridor (Clause 58.07-2 / 58.07-3).

items.title: BADS — setback, outlook and internal views
items.detail: Set the building back to the zone, overlay and BADS outlook standards. Limit views into existing and proposed private open space and habitable rooms (more than 50% of the space). Check building separation for daylight between wings.

items.title: BADS — dwelling storage
items.detail: Each dwelling needs convenient, usable and secure storage to the BADS volume table (internal plus external or in a store). Do not count hanging-rail wardrobe space as the storage volume.

items.title: Orientation for 7-star NatHERS
items.detail: Lock living-room solar access, glazing areas, shading and thermal mass so a 7-star NatHERS outcome is plausible. Victoria’s 7-star and whole-of-home requirements continue under NCC 2025, in force from 1 May 2026.

items.title: Livable housing path of travel
items.detail: Plan a step-free path, entrance width, and adaptable bathroom location. For Class 2, at least 50% of dwellings must meet the NCC livable housing provisions (or the higher VPP standard where it applies).

items.title: Parking, crossovers and waste
items.detail: Check Clause 52.06 parking, crossover locations, visitor parking, and whether waste collection is kerbside or on-site.

items.title: Client sign-off of preferred concept
items.detail: Written approval of the preferred concept, with a cost check against the brief, before design development.

items.title: Coordinated GA drawings
items.detail: Plans, sections and elevations at a scale suitable for planning, with levels, materials, and adjoining interfaces.

items.title: Consultant team engaged
items.detail: Appoint as needed: land surveyor, structural, civil/hydraulic, energy assessor, landscape, ESD, fire, acoustic, traffic, waste, geotech, quantity surveyor.
references: ARBV Code of Professional Conduct — competence and consultants

items.title: Preliminary NatHERS and whole-of-home
items.detail: Run a preliminary 7-star rating and whole-of-home assessment. Adjust fabric before planning freeze.

items.title: Stormwater and permeability
items.detail: STORM or MUSIC assessment, on-site detention if required, and permeability consistent with the planning standard.

items.title: Overlooking, overshadowing and daylight
items.detail: Prepare diagrams for overlooking, overshadowing of secluded private open space, daylight to existing windows, and protection of existing rooftop solar.

items.title: Landscape and deep soil
items.detail: Landscape concept with canopy trees, deep-soil volumes, and front-garden character. Apartments: deep-soil / canopy tables in 55.07 or 58.03.

items.title: BADS — deep soil and canopy
items.detail: Provide canopy cover over deep-soil areas to the BADS landscaping table (Clause 58.03-5 / 55.07-4). Retain existing trees where possible; replace significant trees removed in the 12 months before lodgement. Show soil volume, depth and species, not only a planting image.

items.title: ESD / BESS (apartments and larger townhouse sites)
items.detail: Where council policy requires it, prepare a BESS or equivalent ESD report covering energy, water, IEQ, stormwater and waste.

items.title: BADS — wind impacts
items.detail: For five storeys or more (excluding a basement), demonstrate comfortable and safe wind conditions on public land, communal open space and private open space. Commission a qualified wind assessment where the standard requires it.

items.title: BADS — noise impacts
items.detail: Keep plant away from bedrooms. Address road and rail noise, apartment-to-apartment transfer, and specified internal noise levels on busy transport corridors (Clause 58.04-3).

items.title: BADS — building entry and circulation
items.detail: Give the building a clear street identity. Entries, corridors, lifts and stairs should be visible, sheltered and sized for furniture and people with limited mobility (Clause 58.05-2).

items.title: BADS — natural ventilation
items.detail: Maximise openable windows and doors. At least 40% of dwellings should have effective cross-ventilation with a complying breeze path (Clause 58.07-4).

items.title: BADS — external walls and materials
items.detail: Specify durable external walls that weather well and suit the urban context. The design response must explain the finish selection (Clause 58.06-4 / 55.07-19).

items.title: BADS — accessible dwellings
items.detail: At least 50% of dwellings should meet BADS accessibility (850 mm entries, clear path to the main bedroom and bathroom, bathroom circulation). Align this set with the NCC livable-housing 50% for Class 2.

items.title: Waste management plan
items.detail: Apartment (and larger townhouse) waste rooms, collection vehicle path, and council waste policy.

items.title: Client approval to lodge planning
items.detail: Confirm the scheme, cost update, and authority to lodge with council (or to proceed to building permit if no planning permit is required).

items.title: Confirm whether a planning permit is required
items.detail: Single dwellings on lots without overlays often proceed on a building permit only. Dual occupancy, townhouses, apartments, overlays and demolition commonly need a planning permit.

items.title: Clause 54 assessment (house)
items.detail: If a permit is required for one dwelling or a small second dwelling, assess against Clause 54 including neighbourhood character, tree canopy and amenity (VC282 from 8 September 2025).

items.title: Clause 55 assessment (townhouse / low-rise)
items.detail: Meet Clause 55 objectives. Where using deemed-to-comply standards, document each standard met. Otherwise provide an alternative design response against neighbourhood character policy.

items.title: BADS — Clause 58 assessment (5+ storeys)
items.detail: Lodge a Clause 58 assessment covering urban context, site layout, amenity impacts, on-site amenity, detailed design and internal amenity. Meet every objective; where a standard is varied, explain how the objective is still met.

items.title: BADS — Clause 55.07 assessment (under 5 storeys)
items.detail: If the apartment building is under five storeys, assess against Clause 55.07 (and Clause 55 / the Townhouse and Low-Rise Code if three storeys or less). Mark N/A on a project if Clause 58 is the applicable path instead.

items.title: Neighbourhood and site description + design response
items.detail: Prepare the Clause 54.01 / 55.01 package: existing conditions, neighbourhood character and a design response that explains the scheme.

items.title: Planning drawing set
items.detail: Site plan, floor plans, elevations, sections, shadow diagrams, materials, landscape, and development summary (site coverage, permeability, garden area, canopy, parking).

items.title: Supporting reports
items.detail: As required: traffic, waste, ESD/BESS, arborist, heritage, flood, bushfire, urban context, acoustic, wind, affordable housing.

items.title: Lodge application and pay fees
items.detail: Lodge with the responsible authority, keep the application number, and diary statutory clocks.

items.title: Further information and advertising
items.detail: Respond to s54 further information. Track notice/advertising, objectors, and any consultation.

items.title: Planning permit and endorsed plans
items.detail: Receive the permit, read every condition, and obtain endorsed plans. Diary secondary consents, expiry, and plans-to-be-endorsed conditions.

items.title: Subdivision and statement of compliance
items.detail: For townhouses (and apartment lots), run the plan of subdivision, OC schedule, and statement of compliance in parallel with construction as required.

items.title: Match endorsed town planning drawings
items.detail: Check every planning condition and endorsed dimension before issuing a building-permit set. Record any secondary consent needed.

items.title: Working drawings and specification
items.detail: Issue a coordinated architectural set and specification suitable for tender and for the building surveyor.

items.title: NCC 2025 compliance notes
items.detail: Classify the building (Class 1a / 1b / 2 / 7a carpark etc.) and document performance solutions, fire, moisture, energy and accessibility against NCC 2025, in force in Victoria from 1 May 2026. Building work under a permit existing immediately before that date stays on the previous requirements unless the owner and relevant building surveyor agree to apply NCC 2025 (Building Act s 10). Plumbing: PCA 2025, including lead-free WaterMark products.

items.title: Final NatHERS 7-star and whole-of-home
items.detail: Final energy report for the building permit. New permits: NCC 2025 energy (7-star fabric plus whole-of-home). Permits existing before 1 May 2026 may remain on NCC 2022 under Building Act s 10.

items.title: Livable housing details
items.detail: Dimension step-free paths, 850 mm clear entries, sanitary facilities and adaptable bathrooms to the ABCB Livable Housing Design Standard (NCC 2025 Part H8). Apartments: identify the 50% of dwellings that meet Design A or B.

items.title: Condensation management
items.detail: Detail climate-zone vapour permeance, wall membranes, and roof ventilation to NCC 2025. Most of Victoria is climate zone 6: a drained and ventilated wall cavity is required (also zones 7 and 8). Roof ventilation depends on whether insulation is parallel to the roof plane.

items.title: Structural, civil and services drawings
items.detail: Coordinated structure, stormwater, sewer, electrical, mechanical and fire drawings issued as part of the permit set.

items.title: Waterproofing and wet areas
items.detail: Specify AS 3740 wet-area systems, inspection hold points, and AS 4654 external waterproofing for roofs, balconies and terraces over habitable rooms (NCC 2025 Part H2).

items.title: Part 5 siting vs planning permit
items.detail: Where no planning permit exists, check Part 5 of the Building Regulations (siting). Where a planning permit exists, apply regulation 68 so the building permit is not inconsistent with the planning permit.

items.title: Building manual inputs
items.detail: Collect information needed for the building manual / operations information that the 2025 inspection and manual reforms expect at occupancy.
references: Building Amendment (Building Manuals and Mandatory Inspections) Regulations 2025

items.title: Tender set issued
items.detail: Issue drawings, specification, planning permit, and known site constraints. Record tender closing date.

items.title: Tender RFIs
items.detail: Answer builder queries in writing and issue addenda to all tenderers.

items.title: Tender comparison
items.detail: Compare price, program, qualifications, PC sums, and exclusions on the same basis.

items.title: Builder registration and insurance
items.detail: Confirm VBA/BPC registration, domestic building insurance where required, and public liability.

items.title: Building contract executed
items.detail: Execute a written contract (ABIC, HIA or other) with the drawings and spec listed. Architect as contract administrator if engaged for that stage.

items.title: Appoint relevant building surveyor
items.detail: Client appoints a registered building surveyor. Do not let the builder appoint the RBS for the client.

items.title: Building permit issued
items.detail: Building permit received before work starts. Check it lists the correct drawings, stages, and mandatory notification stages.

items.title: Mandatory inspections program
items.detail: Diary foundation, framing, waterproofing, occupancy and any additional 2025 notification stages. Builders must notify the RBS before covering work.

items.title: Site meetings and minutes
items.detail: Minute directions, RFIs, and quality issues. Architect remains impartial if administering the contract.
references: ARBV Code — administer building contracts impartially

items.title: Variations
items.detail: Price and approve variations in writing before the work proceeds. Keep a running cost report.
references: Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act 2002 (Vic)

items.title: Progress claims and certificates
items.detail: Assess claims, issue certificates, and track retention or security under the contract.
references: Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act 2002 (Vic)

items.title: Occupancy permit or final inspection
items.detail: RBS issues an occupancy permit (or certificate of final inspection). Apartments: occupancy before residents move in, typically for the building / each part as applicable.

items.title: Apartment developer bond (if captured)
items.detail: For residential apartment buildings over three storeys with a building permit issued from 1 July 2027, lodge a 2% bond with the BPC before applying for occupancy. Notice to BPC as required. Transitional: regulations from 1 July 2026.

items.title: Owners corporation set-up
items.detail: OC registered, insurance, first meeting, common property schedule, and building manual handed over.

items.title: Practical completion inspection
items.detail: Architect inspects against the contract documents. Major defects delay PC; minor defects go on the list.
references: ARBV Code of Professional Conduct — contract administration

items.title: Defects and incomplete works list
items.detail: Issue a dated list. Builder must close items. Occupancy permit does not waive contractual defects.

items.title: Keys, warranties, as-builts and manuals
items.detail: Collect keys, appliance warranties, cleaning, as-built services drawings, operation manuals, and the building manual.
references: Building Amendment (Building Manuals and Mandatory Inspections) Regulations 2025 (Vic)

items.title: Certificate of practical completion
items.detail: Issue PC. This starts the defects liability period. Record the date in the project JSON.

items.title: Defects liability period diary
items.detail: Record DLP start (PC date) and end. Typical residential contracts use 12 months; check the executed contract.

items.title: Defects register
items.detail: Log each defect with date, location, photo, item id, and close-out date. Empty notes are allowed; do not delete closed items.
references: ARBV Code of Professional Conduct — document and maintain records

items.title: Apartment bond preliminary inspection (15–18 months)
items.detail: If the developer bond scheme applies, arrange the qualified building assessor inspection 15–18 months after occupancy and give the developer an opportunity to rectify.

items.title: Apartment bond final inspection (21–24 months)
items.detail: If the preliminary report still has reportable defects, complete the 21–24 month inspection. OC may then claim on the bond.

items.title: DLP close-out
items.detail: Confirm all listed defects are fixed or accepted. Extend DLP if the contract requires it when items remain open.

items.title: Final inspection after DLP
items.detail: Inspect remaining items. Do not issue a final certificate while contractual defects remain that the builder is obliged to fix.

items.title: Final certificate
items.detail: Issue the final certificate. Domestic building warranty typically covers six years for structural defects and two years for non-structural defects.

items.title: Release retention / security
items.detail: Release remaining security in accordance with the contract after final certificate.
references: Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act 2002 (Vic)

items.title: Archive project records
items.detail: Keep the agreement, permits, endorsed drawings, certificates, and this JSON package. Architects must document and maintain records.
references: ARBV Code — document and maintain records

items.title: Occupant feedback
items.detail: Collect structured feedback after at least one winter and one summer where possible: comfort, storage, daylight, acoustics, operation of systems.

items.title: Energy and condensation check
items.detail: Compare bills or monitoring to the NatHERS intent. Look for condensation in bathrooms, robes and south-facing rooms.

items.title: Landscape establishment
items.detail: Confirm canopy trees and deep-soil planting have established, irrigation works, and any planning landscape condition is still met.
references: Planning and Environment Act 1987 (Vic) permit conditions

items.title: Lessons learned
items.detail: Note what to change on the next Victorian house, townhouse or apartment project. Store against this project, not only in someone’s inbox.
references: ARBV Code of Professional Conduct — document and maintain records

grokbots.name: Brief
grokbots.title: Pre-design researcher
grokbots.description: Turns a Victorian site into a briefing pack: title risks, zone/overlays, Clauses 54 / 55 / 58, and BADS for apartments.
grokbots.firstTask: Using only the attached project JSON and any title or planning-scheme files, produce a pre-design briefing note for this Victoria site. State typology (house, townhouse or apartment), likely planning permit trigger, applicable VPP clause, overlays, and missing surveys. Flag unknowns. Do not contact council. Stop after the note.
approvalRules: Do not lodge permits, pay fees, or send emails to councils, surveyors or neighbours.
Do not modify the project JSON except as a proposed patch presented for approval.
Stop for approval before any external account sign-in, payment, or legal acceptance.

grokbots.name: Sketch
grokbots.title: Concept tester
grokbots.description: Stress-tests a sketch against 7-star orientation, livable housing, parking and the relevant ResCode / BADS envelope.
grokbots.firstTask: Read the project JSON and any concept PDFs. List envelope risks (height, setbacks, canopy, garden area, overlooking) and, for apartments, BADS communal open space, balcony sizes, room depth and functional layout. Return a punch-list mapped to checklist item ids. Do not redraw the scheme unless asked.
approvalRules: Do not lodge permits, pay fees, or send emails to councils, surveyors or neighbours.
Do not modify the project JSON except as a proposed patch presented for approval.
Stop for approval before any external account sign-in, payment, or legal acceptance.

grokbots.name: Resolve
grokbots.title: Design-development coordinator
grokbots.description: Tracks consultants, NatHERS, stormwater and amenity diagrams before a planning freeze.
grokbots.firstTask: From the project JSON, list which design-development checklist items still lack notes. Propose consultant RFPs and a lodging-readiness score. Do not email consultants.
approvalRules: Do not lodge permits, pay fees, or send emails to councils, surveyors or neighbours.
Do not modify the project JSON except as a proposed patch presented for approval.
Stop for approval before any external account sign-in, payment, or legal acceptance.

grokbots.name: Permit
grokbots.title: Planning permit packer
grokbots.description: Assembles a Clause 54 / 55 / 58 lodgement checklist and tracks RFI and permit conditions.
grokbots.firstTask: Using the attached project JSON and template, draft a lodgement completeness list for this typology and storey count. Quote the relevant VPP clause. If a permit is already noted, extract condition types to watch (endorsed plans, landscape, ESD). Do not lodge.
approvalRules: Do not lodge permits, pay fees, or send emails to councils, surveyors or neighbours.
Do not modify the project JSON except as a proposed patch presented for approval.
Stop for approval before any external account sign-in, payment, or legal acceptance.

grokbots.name: Working
grokbots.title: Documentation checker
grokbots.description: Diffs the building-permit set against endorsed planning drawings and NCC 2025 energy, livable housing and condensation.
grokbots.firstTask: Compare notes in the project JSON against NCC 2025 items (7-star, livable housing, condensation, waterproofing). List gaps that would stall a Victorian building permit. Note Building Act s 10 if a pre-1 May 2026 permit still sits on NCC 2022. Do not issue drawings.
approvalRules: Do not lodge permits, pay fees, or send emails to councils, surveyors or neighbours.
Do not modify the project JSON except as a proposed patch presented for approval.
Stop for approval before any external account sign-in, payment, or legal acceptance.

grokbots.name: Tender
grokbots.title: Tender comparitor
grokbots.description: Helps compare builder tenders on a like-for-like basis and checks registration and insurance.
grokbots.firstTask: If tender notes or attachments exist, build a comparison table (price, program, exclusions, PC sums). Confirm the file notes whether the builder is registered and DBI is addressed. Do not appoint a builder.
approvalRules: Do not lodge permits, pay fees, or send emails to councils, surveyors or neighbours.
Do not modify the project JSON except as a proposed patch presented for approval.
Stop for approval before any external account sign-in, payment, or legal acceptance.

grokbots.name: CA
grokbots.title: Contract administrator
grokbots.description: Tracks building permit, inspections, variations and occupancy. Remains impartial.
grokbots.firstTask: Summarise open contract-administration items, including building permit, inspections and variations. For apartments, note whether the 2% developer bond scheme might apply given storeys and permit timing. Do not instruct the builder.
approvalRules: Do not lodge permits, pay fees, or send emails to councils, surveyors or neighbours.
Do not modify the project JSON except as a proposed patch presented for approval.
Stop for approval before any external account sign-in, payment, or legal acceptance.

grokbots.name: PC
grokbots.title: Practical completion inspector
grokbots.description: Turns site notes and photos into a dated defects and incomplete-works list.
grokbots.firstTask: From notes and any attached photos or PDFs, draft a practical completion defects list grouped by location. Mark items that should delay PC versus DLP. Do not certify PC.
approvalRules: Do not lodge permits, pay fees, or send emails to councils, surveyors or neighbours.
Do not modify the project JSON except as a proposed patch presented for approval.
Stop for approval before any external account sign-in, payment, or legal acceptance.

grokbots.name: Defects
grokbots.title: Defects register
grokbots.description: Keeps the DLP register and, for captured apartment buildings, the bond inspection window.
grokbots.firstTask: Rebuild the defects register from answers and notes. Diary DLP end. If typology is apartment and storeys > 3, outline the 15–18 and 21–24 month bond inspections as optional future items. Do not contact the builder.
approvalRules: Do not lodge permits, pay fees, or send emails to councils, surveyors or neighbours.
Do not modify the project JSON except as a proposed patch presented for approval.
Stop for approval before any external account sign-in, payment, or legal acceptance.

grokbots.name: Final
grokbots.title: Final certificate clerk
grokbots.description: Checks DLP close-out, warranty start, and archive completeness.
grokbots.firstTask: Confirm whether DLP close-out notes exist and list the archive (permits, certificates, this JSON package). Draft a final-certificate readiness paragraph. Do not issue the certificate.

grokbots.description: Structures seasonal POE questions and records lessons for the next Victorian residential project.
grokbots.firstTask: Draft a short POE questionnaire tailored to this typology (house, townhouse or apartment) covering winter/summer comfort, energy, condensation, landscape and waste. Do not contact occupants.
